Intro to Linux KVM (Kernel Based Virtualization) and its Benefits

Dude... I've been runing ESXi in my home lab for years, and I thought it was the bees knees. Of course, we run it at work, too; very high capacity stuff, with licensing out the wazoo.

But ho-lee-crap... I recently decided to rebuild my home lab based around KVM because, well, I was bored, and even on the exact same hardware it's noticeably faster; peppier. I'm able to get away with standing up virtual instances with far smaller footprints than I could with VMWare.

And it's given me a lot of hands-on knowledge about Linux networking where before I only had conceptual knowledge. I made a lot of mistakes and had a lot of frustration trying to get a cloudstack/openstack environment working some time ago, and I realize now, working more closely with the virtualization layer of the stack, that I had a fundamental misunderstanding of some of the key concepts. I feel that I can now go back to that effort and make headway, all thanks to KVM.
